_README.purpose: Curated map: catalogue entry -> proprietary products it can replace. Inverts the lookup so a buyer can start from an invoice line rather than from a solution.
_README.status: CURATED AND PARTIAL. Hand-seeded, not exhaustive, not authoritative. Absence of a mapping is NOT evidence that no replacement exists.
_README.keyed_by: catalogue entry name, matched case-insensitively. `qid` is recorded where known so a rename upstream does not silently orphan the mapping. export_json.py WARNS on keys that match nothing, so this file cannot rot unnoticed.

confidence.strong: like-for-like functional substitute for the common use case
confidence.partial: covers the main use case with real gaps
confidence.adjacent: same domain, different shape - needs a workflow change

kind.service: the paid item is a hosted SERVICE or CONTENT subscription; self-hosting this replaces the software but you still need hosting/content. Drupal does not replace hosting; Moodle does not produce training content.
kind.paid-tier: the paid item is a commercial edition of software that is ALREADY open source. Usually the cheapest win in a procurement review - often no migration at all, just a licence you stop renewing.

_README.how_to_extend: Add entries here, or declare them upstream in publiccode.yml as a top-level `replaces:` list (non-standard extension; harvest.py picks it up if present so publishers can own their own claims).

Icinga.note: Icinga2 is a fork of Nagios and runs Nagios plugins, but XI's bundled web UI, reporting and config wizards are a real gap. For a no-migration exit from XI see the Nagios (Core) entry.

Elasticsearch.note: This entry itself is SSPL-1.0 + Elastic Licence 2.0, i.e. NOT OSI-approved. For a fully open successor use OpenSearch.

RapidPro.note: Closes a gap reported as empty: RapidPro is a flow-based SMS/IVR platform used by governments at national scale.

GOV.UK Notify.note: Email, SMS and letters for public bodies; the service the UK runs at national scale.

KoboToolbox.note: Closes a gap reported as empty.

display-admin-client.note: OS2Display, Danish municipal digital signage. Closes a gap reported as empty.

Mautic.note: NOT a social scheduling replacement. Mautic does campaigns and automation; it does not schedule social posts. Recorded as adjacent so it is not mistaken for closing that gap.

Grammalecte.note: French-language grammar checking; not a like-for-like English replacement.

OS2mo.product: organisation and identity master data management

Apache HTTP Server.note: IIS ships with Windows Server, so the saving is the Windows Server licence only if the host moves too.

CentOS.note: CentOS Stream is now UPSTREAM of RHEL, not a rebuild of it, so this is no longer the like-for-like swap CentOS Linux used to be. For a RHEL-compatible rebuild see Rocky Linux.

ClamAV.note: ClamAV covers mail and file scanning, NOT endpoint protection: no EDR, behavioural detection or central policy. Do not scope it as an EPP swap.

Drupal.note: Headless SaaS CMS. Drupal replaces the authoring software, not the hosting.

Geonetwork.note: GeoNetwork covers the metadata catalogue and discovery portal, not the wider ArcGIS server stack. For the map server see GeoServer.

Hedgedoc.note: HedgeDoc is the community fork of HackMD; the paid item is the hosted service.

Katello.note: Satellite IS Foreman plus Katello, productised and supported.

Krita.note: Krita targets digital painting; Photoshop's photo-retouching and prepress features are the gap. For those see GIMP.

Kubernetes.note: OpenShift is built on Kubernetes but adds an opinionated platform layer (build pipelines, routes, RBAC defaults, support). Dropping to upstream Kubernetes means rebuilding that layer, so this is not a free swap.

MISP.note: MISP is the sharing platform, not the intelligence feed. The subscription buys content; MISP does not produce it.

Nagios.note: Nagios XI is the commercial edition built on Nagios Core, so this is a licence you stop renewing rather than a migration - at the cost of XI's web UI, reporting and config wizards.

OpenLdap.note: AD is directory plus Kerberos, Group Policy and Windows domain join. For the domain-controller role see Samba.

podman.note: Docker Desktop requires a paid subscription for larger organisations; Podman Desktop is a drop-in for the common build/run workflow.

Postfix.note: Postfix is the SMTP layer only. Exchange also provides mailboxes, calendaring and Outlook integration - see Dovecot for IMAP and a groupware suite for the rest.

RStudio.note: Formerly RStudio Server Pro. The desktop IDE is already open source.

SuiteCRM.note: SuiteCRM forked SugarCRM Community Edition when Sugar closed it.

VeraCrypt.note: BitLocker ships with Windows, so the saving is usually the management tooling rather than a licence line.

Wordpress.note: Replaces the site-building software; hosting still has to come from somewhere.
